verdict.rationale: Semgrep's homepage claims it can 'Scan and fix AI-generated code the moment it's written'. A probe confirms an official MCP server is documented, which is the mechanism for wiring the scanner into a coding agent. The documented pre-commit integration also catches issues before they enter Git history. However, the pack has no detail on how the MCP server or an agent hook is configured, what it scans, or whether it gates code before it lands. Missing for 10: documented agent/MCP setup and tool details, evidence of blocking or gating AI-generated changes from the agent loop, independent hands-on corroboration of the agent integration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can wire the scanner into my coding agent so AI-generated code is scanned for issues before it lands

citations.quote: Scan and fix AI-generated code the moment it's written
official MCP server documented at https://docs.semgrep.dev/mcp
The pre-commit framework can run semgrep when you commit changes. This is helpful in preventing secrets and security issues from leaking into your Git history.
